title: SSE chunking/backpressure debug notes (Devon)
content:
Quick notes + repro attempts for the intermittent streaming issues observed on staging (SSE/Transfer-Encoding: chunked). Mostly a scratchpad; fragmented.

Summary:
- Intermittent stalls / long pauses mid-stream when client is slow or when downstream network has jitter.
- Sometimes server drops connection after ~30s of stall with: "stream canceled" or "connection reset by peer" on client side.
- Other times client receives duplicated tokens (observed twice in sequence) after reconnection.
- Issue more visible on model xlarge-quant (longer generation) but reproducible with small generative prompts too.

Observed on:
- Node fetch (undici / native) and browser Fetch streaming consuming SSE events.
- Python aiohttp streaming client.
- curl --no-buffer shows visible chunk boundaries but timing varies.

Hypotheses:
1) Runtime emits very small chunks (1-2 tokens) causing high syscalls; under backpressure the event loop/IO becomes congested and stall occurs.
2) Our HTTP keepalive/read deadlines conflict with client slowness -> runtime treats slow reader as dead and cancels request.
3) SSE framing + gzip/deflate buffering causes buffered data to not flush until larger chunk; mixing chunked + compression + small writes can be flaky.
4) KV cache flush / batching happening mid-stream that pauses generation while kernel swap occurs.

Repro steps tried (commands):
1) CURL baseline (fastest):
   curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"xlarge-quant","prompt":"repeat: token"}' \
     https://api.internal.redwood/v1/stream
   Notes: -N / --no-buffer shows chunk timing. Observed ~3-8s pause after ~120 tokens.

2) Node repro (undici streaming + artificial slow consumer):
   // run server simul; client.js
   const { request } = require('undici');
   const res = await request('https://api.internal.redwood/v1/stream', {
     method: 'POST',
     headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json', 'accept': 'text/event-stream' },
     body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'xlarge-quant', prompt: 'loop many tokens' })
   });
   const reader = res.body.getReader();
   // intentionally slow read
   while (true) {
     const { done, value } = await reader.read();
     if (done) break;
     await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 200)); // 200ms pause per chunk
     process.stdout.write(value);
   }
   Observed: After ~20s, reader.read() hangs indefinitely. Connection eventually resets.

3) Node with Fast consumer (no artificial delay):
   same as above with 0ms delay. Stream completes normally.

4) Python aiohttp slow consumer:
   async with session.post(url, json=payload) as resp:
     async for chunk in resp.content.iter_chunked(1024):
       await asyncio.sleep(0.15) # slow
       handle(chunk)
   Observed similar hangs but less frequent than node; sometimes stream recovers after a long pause and emits backlog tokens.

Server logs (selected snippets):
- [2026-02-28T14:22:17.123Z] req_id=abc123 emit chunk size=28 tokens time=14ms
- [2026-02-28T14:22:17.148Z] req_id=abc123 write to conn (fd=72) bytes=512
- [2026-02-28T14:22:22.215Z] req_id=abc123 io_pause_detected duration=5.07s
- [2026-02-28T14:22:22.216Z] req_id=abc123 client-slow-read pause-count=1
- [2026-02-28T14:22:47.450Z] req_id=abc123 connection_closed reason=read-timeout
- Occasionally: "http2: stream canceled" in worker logs for req_id=def456

What I tried / experiments:
- Increased flush frequency on SSE writer (flush after every token vs batch of 8) -> reduced latency but increased CPU and more frequent stalls under load (probably due to syscalls).
- Disabled gzip on response (set Content-Encoding: identity) -> small improvement, fewer stalls in Python client.
- Toggled socket keepalive and read-timeout on server to larger values -> reduced premature cancellations but stalls still present.
- Added exponential backoff on server side when write returns EAGAIN -> seemed to mitigate connection resets but increases total latency massively.

Preliminary conclusions:
- Problem appears to be combination of small-chunk writes + TCP buffering + client-side read slowness.
- Compression interacts poorly (small writes get buffered by compressor). Disabling compression helps.
- Node consumer seems more sensitive (undici/browser) — possibly underlying HTTP2/streams implementation differs.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Reproduce locally with a controlled network emulator (tc/netem) to simulate up to 200ms RTT, 1% packet loss, and slow recv window.
- Add server-side instrumentation to measure write syscall return codes and kernel send buffer occupancy. Log SO_SNDBUF usage per conn.
- Try using SSE no-framing: send plain chunked text (no "data: ..." prefix) to see if SSE framing is culprit.
- Evaluate switch to HTTP/1.1 chunked only & disable http2 for streaming endpoints as an experiment.
- Add integration test that spawns a slow consumer and asserts server does not cancel connection; use headless Node + netem in CI.
- Reach out to Kyla (networking) for tcp tuning guidance; Samir for runtime kernel/epoll behavior.

Notes for potential quick fixes (short-term):
- For now, set response header Content-Encoding: identity for streaming endpoints to avoid compressor buffering.
- Increase server read-timeout to 120s for streaming endpoints.
- Add a server-side heartbeat SSE comment (": keepalive\n\n") every 10s to keep connection alive and detect slow readers earlier.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do duplicate tokens appear after reconnects? Race when generator resumed + partial buffer? Need to capture generator state around cancellation.
- Is there a kernel-level bug on our GPU hosts when send buffer fills that causes streams to be aborted?
- Which client implementations handle backpressure correctly (pull-based) vs those that rely on internal buffering?

Scratch log (timestamps local):
- 2026-02-27 10:15AM: first noticed while testing canary with slow stream consumer.
- 2026-02-27 17:40PM: reproduced with undici slow read.
- 2026-02-28 14:22:22: captured server pause logs and connection_closed.

Useful commands for future repro runs:
- curl with simulated slow read (pv):
   curl -s -N ... | pv -qL 10 # throttle output to 10 bytes/s to emulate slow client
- netem to add delay/loss on local machine (requires sudo):
   sudo tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 100ms loss 1%
- wrk or vegeta for load tests but need streaming-aware clients; consider custom k6 script that reads streaming responses.

Notes-to-self: capture a full tcpdump (pcap) when reproducing to see retransmits and window sizes. Use req_id in logs to correlate.

-- end of scratchpad --

If I make progress I'll move items into a proper ticket and add more structured reproducer (node script + docker netem).
